The project has been running a long, extremely thorough "100% kubelet parity" gap-closure effort tracked entirely in /workspace/not-k8s/docs/GAP_CLOSURE.md — currently at "Round 102". That doc is your primary reference: read its "## Verified scope boundary" section near the top (confirms what's genuinely NOT kubelet's job — scheduler, controller-manager, cloud-controller-manager, apiserver admission, etcd, kube-proxy equivalent already reimplemented, Windows support) and skim the reverse-chronological "## Round N: ..." sections to see what's already been found and closed (105KB+ file — read it in chunks with offset/limit, don't try to load it all at once; grep for section headers first with `grep -n "^## Round" docs/GAP_CLOSURE.md`).

YOUR TASK: find genuinely new, currently-undocumented parity gaps between nodelet and real kubelet — a "fresh gap re-audit" round, following the exact same methodology as ~13 prior audit rounds in this doc (rounds 22, 27, 35, 39, 45, 50, 54, 58, 72, 76, 80, 83, 86, 89, 92 — read a few of these sections directly, e.g. lines 545-591 for round 92 and 827-880 for round 86, to see the exact tone/rigor/format expected). Audit-only: do NOT write or edit any code. Do NOT create a plan. Just investigate and report back.

WHAT'S ALREADY BEEN SWEPT CLEAN (do not re-report these as new findings unless you find something the swept pass actually missed):
- k8s-openapi struct field sweeps (every field checked against whether nodelet's code references it): `PodSpec`, `Container`, `PodStatus` (round 86), `ContainerStatus` (round 89), `NodeStatus`, `NodeSpec`, `Probe`, `PodSecurityContext`, container-level `SecurityContext`, `NodeSystemInfo`, `Lifecycle`, `ResourceRequirements`, `ContainerResizePolicy` (round 92).
- Full vendored `proto/cri.proto` field-declaration sweep (round 83) plus manual passes on CRI's `Mount` message fields (rounds 76/78/80/82/83).
- Feature areas already confirmed implemented or explicitly out-of-scope by specific past rounds: gRPC probes, oom_score_adj, native sidecar containers (init container restartPolicy:Always), hostPID/hostIPC/shareProcessNamespace, securityContext.sysctls, in-place pod vertical scaling (resize subresource), volume source kinds (all of them — checked via `volume_source_type()`'s match arms), startup-probe failure handling, local ephemeral storage, imagePullPolicy enforcement, CRI's Status/Version RPCs, PodStatus.qosClass, hugepages (container limits + capacity/allocatable + emptyDir.medium), supplementalGroupsPolicy, Dynamic Resource Allocation, activeDeadlineSeconds, hostPort, mountPropagation, recursiveReadOnly (both directions), observedGeneration, Mount.uidMappings/gidMappings, ContainerStatus.user, crash-loop backoff, PodResources API, allocatedResourcesStatus, procMount, raw block volumes, TLS bootstrap/CSR issuance, client cert auth, --config file support, fsGroupChangePolicy, eviction (QoS+priority+exceedsRequests tiebreak chain, soft/hard threshold grace periods), /metrics/cadvisor (5 usage metrics + last_seen + network I/O as of round 102), device plugins, CPU/Memory/Topology managers, CSI (PVC path, ephemeral inline, attach coordination, dynamic driver discovery, secrets), user namespaces, terminationMessagePath/Policy, readinessGates, ConfigMap/Secret live-update, native sidecars, hostname/subdomain/setHostnameAsFQDN, env resourceFieldRef, probe terminationGracePeriodSeconds, image credential providers, image GC watermark policy, subPath $(VAR) expansion, swap support, lifecycle.stopSignal, hostPath volumes, Node.status.images/runtimeHandlers/volumesInUse/volumesAttached/hostIPs, containerID scheme prefix, ContainerStatus.lastState, PodCondition.observedGeneration.

1. k8s-openapi struct fields NOT yet swept: look at `Volume`/`VolumeSource` variant-level fields (round 45 checked which volume *kinds* are handled, but did it check every field *within* each handled kind, e.g. every ConfigMapVolumeSource/SecretVolumeSource/DownwardAPIVolumeSource field?), `EnvVar`/`EnvVarSource`/`EnvFromSource`, `EphemeralContainer` specifically (as its own struct, not just via the Container-conversion path), `PodDNSConfig`, `TypedLocalObjectReference` usages, `ClaimSource/ResourceClaim`-adjacent PodSpec fields beyond what DRA rounds covered.
2. Kubelet's own CLI flags / config knobs from the reference doc (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kubelet/) that haven't been checked yet — e.g. --serialize-image-pulls, --max-parallel-image-pulls, --registry-qps/--registry-burst, --event-qps/--event-burst, --image-pull-progress-deadline, --runtime-request-timeout, --housekeeping-interval, --sync-frequency, --node-lease-duration-seconds, --make-iptables-util-chains, --cgroup-driver, --cgroups-per-qos, --enforce-node-allocatable, --protect-kernel-defaults, --seccomp-default, --pod-max-pids, --rotate-server-certificates (vs the already-closed client cert rotation), --contention-profiling. 3. Kubelet's HTTP server surface (real kubelet exposes /healthz, /metrics, /metrics/cadvisor, /metrics/resource, /metrics/probes, /pods, /runningpods, /stats/*, /spec/, /logs/, /run/, /exec/, /attach/, /portForward/, /containerLogs/, /debug/pprof/, /configz) — check `crates/nodelet/src/server*` (or wherever the HTTP server lives — grep for it) against this list for endpoints never implemented at all that a real scraper/tool might expect.

Any newer (1.30+) kubelet features not yet mentioned anywhere in GAP_CLOSURE.md at all — cross-check against current kubernetes.io docs if you have web access; if not, rely on your own knowledge of recent kubelet features (e.g. user namespaces idmap mounts refinements, image volume source refinements, structured logging, in-place resize refinements, node swap refinements).

Report back a structured summary (it will be used to write a new "## Round 103: fresh gap re-audit" section in the doc) — no need to be exhaustive prose, but be concrete and cite file paths / line numbers / proto message names for every claim. Do not modify any files.

# kubelet parity gap closure — working memory

Started 2026-07-30, rescoped 2026-07-30 (same day, scope expanded from "close
3 known gaps" to "100% kubelet parity, performance-focused"). Checkpoint
commit before this rescoping: `fdf003b`.

## Verified scope boundary (checked against kubernetes.io docs, not assumed)

Sources: [Kubernetes Components](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/components/),
[kubelet reference](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kubelet/),
[Node-pressure eviction](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/node-pressure-eviction/),
[Graceful Node Shutdown](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/21/graceful-node-shutdown-beta/),
[Static Pods](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/static-pod/).

**Confirmed genuinely NOT kubelet's job** (someone else's component, not a
nodelet gap):
- Pod scheduling/binding decisions → **kube-scheduler**.
- etcd storage, Raft quorum, peer election → **etcd**.
- ReplicaSet/Deployment/StatefulSet/Job/CronJob/HPA control loops → **kube-controller-manager**.
- Node lifecycle taints after missed heartbeats, cloud taint lifecycle → **kube-controller-manager** (nodelet already correctly does the one thing that *is* its job here: clearing the `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized` taint on itself — see `node.rs::clear_cloudprovider_taint`).
- Cloud load balancer / route provisioning → **cloud-controller-manager**.
- Admission control, webhooks, server-side apply field management → **kube-apiserver**.
- CSR approval / cluster CA signing → **kube-controller-manager** + **kube-apiserver**.
- Dynamic PV provisioning → external CSI provisioner sidecar (not kubelet); kubelet's actual job here is only the node-local `NodeStageVolume`/`NodePublishVolume` mount, which *is* in scope below.
- Service/Endpoints → **kube-proxy**'s job in stock Kubernetes; nodelet already reimplements this itself (`svc.rs`, nftables) as a deliberate architectural choice predating this doc — stays as-is, not touched by this pass.
- Windows node support — out of scope for a different reason: this project is Linux-only edge hardware by design (cgroup v2, `/proc`, Linux CRI sockets), not "someone else's job."

Everything else below **is** kubelet's job and is now in scope.

## Round 100: `/metrics/cadvisor` gains `container_last_seen` (2026-08-01, same day)

Last of the 4 closeable 🟡 items ("do them all, let's get it
done" — rounds 97-100). `render_cadvisor_metrics()` (`server::prom_metrics`)
gains a fifth metric, `container_last_seen`, alongside its existing
four. Unlike the other four (each gated on `Some(value)` — a real,
possibly-missing measurement), `container_last_seen` is unconditional:
a container's mere presence in a fresh `ListPodSandboxStats` snapshot
already proves it was observed *right now*, so reporting the current
wall-clock time for every container needs no new data collection at
all — a scraper uses this to detect a container that's vanished since
the last scrape (its `last_seen` stops advancing), real cAdvisor's own
actual use for the metric.

`render_cadvisor_metrics()` took `now_unix_seconds: u64` as a new
parameter rather than reading `SystemTime::now()` internally, keeping
it a pure, clock-independent function unit-testable without mocking
time — `handle_metrics_cadvisor()` supplies the real value the same
`SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)` pattern already used
elsewhere in this codebase (`container_state.rs`, `events_gc.rs`).

**Re-confirmed, not just carried over, that network/disk I/O and
per-cpu-core breakdowns stay out of scope**: unlike `container_last_seen`
(a pure formatting/framing gap — the data to report it already
existed implicitly), those need CRI data this codebase genuinely
doesn't collect anywhere today, and spec/limit metrics would need
cross-referencing every container against its Pod's resource spec on
every scrape — both real, separate pieces of work, not something this
round's "closeable" characterization was claiming to cover. The
`/metrics/cadvisor` bullet stays 🟡, correctly.

1 new unit test plus one existing test updated for the new
unconditional metric and the new function signature
(`prom_metrics_tests/render_cadvisor_metrics.rs`). Existing
`test_metrics_cadvisor_returns_real_container_usage`
(`deploy/lib/test/cases/prom_metrics.sh`) extended with
`container_last_seen` TYPE-line and sample-line assertions — no new
test needed since it already stands up a real pod and scrapes the
live endpoint.

This closes all 4 of the user's "do them all" closeable 🟡 items
(rounds 97-100). Remaining below full ✅: the explicitly-not-
recommended Checkpoint API (❌), the 5 DRA/CSI-driver-validation 🟡
items (genuinely infra-blocked, not missing code — the new `e2e.yml`
GitHub Actions workflow, added mid-round-97, gives a path to
eventually closing those for real once a suitable test driver is
wired into it), and whatever narrower simplifications remain within
Eviction/`/metrics/cadvisor`/DRA/PVC-CSI's own 🟡 bullets that this
round's specifically-named sub-gaps didn't claim to fully resolve.

## Round 102: `/metrics/cadvisor` gains network I/O (2026-08-02)

## Round 103 fresh gap re-audit — findings

**Method**: Continued the field-sweep technique on structs not yet swept (`EphemeralContainer`, `PodDNSConfig`, `EnvVar`/`EnvVarSource`/`EnvFromSource`, and the volume-source sub-structs `ConfigMapVolumeSource`/`SecretVolumeSource`/`DownwardAPIVolumeSource`/`KeyToPath`, all read directly from the vendored k8s-openapi 0.28.0 `v1_33` source), then checked the kubelet CLI-flag list against `config.rs`, and the kubelet HTTP surface against `server/routes.rs`.

### Confirmed genuine, undocumented gaps (ranked by value)

1. **Plain `configMap`/`secret` volumes ignore `.items` (`KeyToPath` select+rename)** — `runtime/cri/volumes_resolve.rs:36-70` calls `write_volume_dir(&vol_dir, obj.data, obj.binary_data...)` (`runtime/cri/volumes_pure.rs:558-568`), which unconditionally dumps every key as a file and never even receives `cm.items`/`sec.items`. Compare the `projected` volume path at `volumes_resolve.rs:285-300`, which correctly threads `cm.items.as_deref()`/`sec.items.as_deref()` into `write_projected_keys()` (`volumes_pure.rs:604+`). The code's own doc comment at `volumes_pure.rs:598-603` even says this is a known discrepancy ("...real Kubernetes semantics that plain top-level configMap/secret volumes also have but nodelet doesn't apply there yet (see docs/GAP_CLOSURE.md)") — but it was never actually added to the doc. High real-world value: renaming/selecting a single key (e.g. mounting one key at a specific path like `conf.d/nginx.conf`, or exposing only `ca.crt` from a multi-key secret) is a very common plain-volume pattern, not just a `projected`-volume one. Moderate fix size: `write_volume_dir` needs an `items` parameter and the same per-item logic `write_projected_keys` already has.

2. **`defaultMode`/`KeyToPath.mode` (file permission bits) never applied to any volume-projected file** — none of `ConfigMapVolumeSource.default_mode`, `SecretVolumeSource.default_mode`, `DownwardAPIVolumeSource.default_mode`, or `KeyToPath.mode` are referenced anywhere in the crate (`grep -rn default_mode src/` returns nothing). `write_volume_dir`, `write_projected_keys`, and `write_downward_api_volume` (`volumes_pure.rs:558-640`) all call plain `std::fs::write(...)` with no follow-up `set_permissions`/`chmod` — contrast with the hostPath-volume code path a few lines above (`volumes_pure.rs:48,65`) which does correctly hardcode `0o755`/`0o644` via `PermissionsExt`. Real value: can't mount an executable script from a ConfigMap (a common init/sidecar pattern needing the `+x` bit) and can't restrict a sensitive Secret file to `0400`/`0600` — both real, common manifests that silently get wrong permissions today. Small-to-moderate fix: after each `fs::write`, apply the resolved mode (item-level `mode` overriding the source's `default_mode`, defaulting to `0644` matching upstream).

3. **`/metrics/probes` endpoint not implemented at all** — `server/routes.rs`'s `Route` enum only has `ContainerLogs`/`Exec`/`Attach`/`PortForward`/`StatsSummary`/`MetricsResource`/`MetricsCadvisor`; there's no `["metrics", "probes"]` arm. Real kubelet exposes `probe_success`-style Prometheus gauges here. This one is nearly free to add: `ProbeTracker` (`probes.rs:161-186`) already tracks `passing`/`failures` per container in memory for the threshold state machine — the data this endpoint needs already exists, same shape as round 100's `container_last_seen` win (data already collected, purely a formatting/exposition gap). High value for anyone running Prometheus against nodelet who wants probe-failure alerting without polling pod status via the apiserver.

4. **Unbounded image-pull concurrency (`--serialize-image-pulls`/`--max-parallel-image-pulls` have no nodelet equivalent)** — `pods.rs:274` spawns one `tokio::spawn` task per pod sync with no `Semaphore` or other concurrency gate anywhere in the pull path (`runtime/cri/container_create.rs:249-271`, `container_support.rs:297+`); confirmed via `grep -rn Semaphore` returning nothing in `pods.rs`/`runtime/cri.rs`/`runtime/mod.rs`. Real kubelet defaults to serializing pulls (or bounding them via `--max-parallel-image-pulls`) specifically to avoid disk-I/O thrashing on constrained hardware — directly relevant to this project's own "edge single-node" target profile (per project memory). A node coming back up with many static/mirror pods simultaneously wanting to pull would currently do so with fully unbounded concurrency. Moderate fix: a `tokio::sync::Semaphore` around the `PullImage` call, sized from a new config knob (default matching upstream's serialize-by-default behavior, i.e. permit count 1).

5. **No `--seccomp-default` equivalent — containers with no explicit `seccompProfile` get zero syscall filtering** — `runtime/cri/resources.rs:411-424`'s `seccomp_profile()` returns `None` when neither pod- nor container-level `securityContext.seccompProfile` is set, which leaves CRI's `seccomp` field unset (→ runtime's own default, typically `Unconfined` for containerd). Real kubelet's `--seccomp-default` flag (GA 1.27+) flips this default to `RuntimeDefault` for any container that doesn't explicitly opt out, and is an increasingly standard secure-by-default posture. Given this project has already implemented several other security-hardening features (user namespaces, `oom_score_adj`, etc.), this is a real, in-scope gap, not a cosmetic one. Small fix: a config flag that changes `seccomp_profile()`'s `None` fallback to `RuntimeDefault` instead of leaving the field unset.

### Lower-priority / noted but not ranked as actionable this round
- `/healthz`, `/configz`, `/pods`, `/runningpods` are also entirely absent from `server/routes.rs`'s `Route` enum. Real but lower value than `/metrics/probes`: the Node Lease (already correctly implemented in `node.rs` — `LEASE_NS`/`renew_lease()`, GA lease-based heartbeat, not a gap) already gives the cluster a liveness signal, and these are mostly local-debugging conveniences.
- `--pod-max-pids` (per-pod PID cgroup limit): genuinely unimplemented, but blocked on the vendored CRI proto — `pids_limit` is not a field in `proto/cri.proto` at all (confirmed via grep), so this needs a proto change first, not just application code. Flagged for awareness, not ranked as this round's pick since it's infra-blocked like the DRA/CSI items already called out in Round 100.
- Node Lease duration (`LEASE_DURATION_SECS = 40` in `node.rs:25`) isn't configurable via env, but it already matches upstream's own default of 40s — excluded per this round's instructions (not a behavioral gap, just a hardcoded-to-a-sane-value knob).
- `EphemeralContainer.targetContainerName` was checked and found already deliberately handled as a documented no-op (`runtime/cri/sandbox.rs:75-80`) — nodelet always shares the sandbox's PID namespace across all containers already, so this isn't a fresh finding.
- `PodDNSConfig` (nameservers/searches/options) and `EnvVar`/`EnvVarSource`/`EnvFromSource` (including `EnvFromSource.prefix`) swept clean — all referenced in `runtime/cri/env.rs`.

### Ranking for next round
`configMap`/`secret` plain-volume `.items` support (#1) and `defaultMode`/`KeyToPath.mode` (#2) are the highest-value, most concretely-scoped picks — both are common real-world manifest patterns with a confirmed, precise code location and a small-to-moderate fix. `/metrics/probes` (#3) is the cheapest win (data already in memory, same pattern as round 100). Image-pull concurrency (#4) and `--seccomp-default` (#5) are real but slightly broader/architectural changes.
